findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the uploaded vendor roster) are stored without an enforced default encryption policy.
No acl or public access block is declared for this bucket, leaving access control to defaults and providing no explicit guarantee the bucket and its objects are private.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be overwritten or the entire bucket destroyed with no recoverable prior versions, undermining data integrity protections.
No logging block is configured, so access to this bucket holding exported reports and the vendor roster is not auditable.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial export data is stored without enforced server-side encryption.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, allowing silent overwrite or deletion of ledger export data with no recovery path.
No server access logging is configured for the ledger export bucket, leaving no audit trail of reads or writes to financial data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is declared, so model artifacts are stored without enforced encryption at rest, unlike the audit bucket which uses KMS.
The runbooks bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block; operational runbooks frequently contain sensitive procedural and connection detail and are stored unencrypted by default.
No logging block is configured for the runbooks bucket, so access to it is not recorded for audit or incident investigation.

The acl value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid S3 canned ACL (the intended value appears to be "log-delivery-write"), so the intended access control on the audit log destination bucket will not be applied as expected.
force_destroy = true on the audit trail bucket permits Terraform to delete the bucket and all retained audit logs, weakening tamper-resistance and non-repudiation of security records.
